To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface area of the carbonaceous electrodes has a positive impact on the capacitances of the capacitors.
the surface roughness of carbon-based electrodes has a good impact in the capacitance and that the breakdown voltage of hybrid capacitor is strongly affected by the dielectric material.
the capacitance of a hybrid capacitor is directly linked with the surface area of the electrode, the breakdown voltage of a hybrid capacitor depends on the surface area and the dielectric material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of hybrid capacitors with different carbonaceous electrodes and dielectric materials.
the influence of surface roughness of carbonaceous materials on the capacitance and breakdown voltages for hybrid capacitors.
the study of the influence of the surface roughness of carbonaceous materials (activated carbon and carbon nanotube) on the capacitance and breakdown strength.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increase of the surface roughness of carbonaceous electrodes is beneficial to the increase of capacitance, but the increase of surface roughness of electrodes has a negative impact on the breakdown voltage.
the surface roughness is an important parameter to increase the capacitances of hybrid capacitors, while preserving the breakdown voltage of the system.
, the surface area of the carbonaceous electrodes is the main factor for increasing the capacitance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the capacitance of the hybrid capacitor can be improved by increasing the surface area of electrodes, but the breakdown voltage is reduced.
the hybrid capacitors are promising devices to improve the capacitance and energy density.
the hybrid capacitors with CNTs electrodes and the dielectric impregnation of polypropylene have a high potential for future application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid capacitors can have a capacitance higher than 10 F cm−3 and a breakdown voltage of 1 kV cm−1, which makes it possible to envisage a new generation of capacitors.
the surface roughness of carbonaceous materials can be a useful tool to increase the capacitances and the breakdown voltages of the hybrid capacitors.
the capacitance and energy storage capability of the proposed hybrid capacitors are higher than the ones of the ultracapacistors.
